messages:
anna: Quick sync — Q3 roadmap item for Dedicated: proposing a 'capacity escrow' model to let customers reserve short-duration burst capacity without full-time overprovisioning. TL;DR: customers buy burst units that sit in a soft pool and can be auto-reclaimed. Need decisions on SLA impact, billing signals, and eviction rules.
sam: +1 conceptually. main worry is tail latency when reclaim happens mid-request. we should prefer graceful downgrade over abrupt kill.
maria: ops ask — define clear tiered windows. gold -> 60s pre-grace, silver -> 30s, bronze -> 5s. also need audit logs for Private/VPC customers.
ricardo: from SRE: prefer deterministic reclaim signals (HTTP 429 w/ Retry-After) rather than silent slowdowns. propose fallback chain: full model -> quantized variant -> queued request -> error. explicit signals will make incident triage easier.
jess: sales note — 2 enterprise customers asked for predictable short bursts with p95 latency guarantees. willing to pay for a premium escrow tier if latency holds.
anna: Proposed launch checklist: (1) reclaim algorithm validated under synthetic spikes, (2) billing + UX for purchasing/consuming escrow units, (3) dashboard + per-tenant tracing, (4) contractual SLA language for escrow tiers, (5) runbook for manual reclaim and customer notifications.
sam: quick prototype policy config sample:
```
autoscale_policy:
  mode: escrow
  initial_pool: dynamic
  reclaim_priority: customer_tier
  grace_window_ms: 2000
  fallback_sequence: [high_perf, quantized, queued]
```
ricardo: perf test plan: simulate 1k concurrent sessions with 20-30s token bursts, measure p50/p95 for each fallback step. target: p95 < 1.5x baseline for gold tier under pilot load.
maria: ops runbook items: how to surface near-exhaustion to customers, automatic top-ups vs manual, escalation path when reclaim fails, and a playbook for rollback. add a monitoring view that shows escrow burn-rate per-minute.
anna: tradeoffs note: tighter isolation and guaranteed lanes increases cost. question: do we accept eventual preemption of other customers (soft-preempt) or only reclaim from a shared pool (no cross-tenant preempt)?
sam: prefer soft-preempt semantics for pilot to limit blast radius — reclaim from ephemeral shared pockets first. if that fails, start tenant-tier preemption with clear signal.
jess: i can negotiate pilot contracts with 3 customers; they want pilot SLA and a clause for rollback. will coordinate legal.
devops-bot: calendar invite created: "Capacity escrow pilot kickoff" Thu Apr 8 10:00 — attendees: anna, sam, maria, ricardo, jess
anna: owners: sam (engineering), maria (ops), ricardo (SRE), jess (sales). OKR alignment: drive Dedicated NRR growth by offering higher-value burst SLAs — target +6% NRR from Dedicated this quarter.
anna: next steps: sam to post design doc and cost model by EOD Fri; maria to draft runbook + monitoring dashboards; ricardo to produce perf matrix and test harness; jess to lock pilot customers and initial contract language.
sam: will post design doc to /docs/dedicated/escrow-proposal.md and include perf scripts. aiming for prototype in 2 sprints.
ricardo: will write the test harness and expected metrics table.
maria: will mock the runbook pages and dashboard widgets.
jess: coordinating customers now.
anna: closing — if no objections by EOD, we'll scope into next planning board and assign tickets. thanks all.
sam: on it.
ricardo: +1
maria: +1
jess: :thumbsup:
